svg.title: P014 · Orders per month in 2025
svg.desc: One row per 2025 month with orders. Order 4 is from December 2024. Orders 1, 2 and 3 remain. January 1 and January 31 both map to 2025-01-01. March 1 maps to 2025-03-01. Orders 1 and 2 form January's group of two. Order 3 forms March's group of one. January totals 100 + 50 = 150. March totals 200. No February group was present in the input. FROM Orders · one table is enough. Each order supplies its month and the amount that month earns. Grouping these transactions produces exactly the months with orders, including both January transactions.
svg.text: One row per 2025 month with orders.
Would February appear if it had no orders?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to

Which orders belong to the reporting year?

g.aria-label: FROM Orders · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Orders · one table is enough
Each order supplies its month and the amount that month earns. Grouping these transactions produces exactly the
months with orders, including both January transactions.

svg.text: Order 4 is from December 2024. Orders 1, 2 and 3 remain.
How can two different January dates share a key?
January 1 and January 31 both map to 2025-01-01. March 1 maps to 2025-03-01.
How many orders belong to each month?
Orders 1 and 2 form January's group of two. Order 3 forms March's group of one.
What is the total value per month?
January totals 100 + 50 = 150. March totals 200. No February group was present in the input.
